edges.description: Loss of a complex I or complex III subunit directly reduces electron transfer through the respiratory chain in cardiac mitochondria.

A respiratory-chain block shifts pyruvate to lactate systemically, giving the raised blood lactate documented in NDUFB11 complex I neonates. It is a mitochondrial-disease marker, and a normal lactate does not exclude the diagnosis.

The subunit defect is not confined to the heart: a case with hypotonia had an independently abnormal skeletal-muscle cytochrome c oxidase assay, so skeletal muscle carries the same respiratory-chain lesion.

The nervous-system and ocular anomalies and the oncocytic cells reported in other glands follow from the same systemic respiratory-chain defect rather than from the cardiac lesion. The intervening steps have never been catalogued, so the edge is kept indirect.
edges.target: Extracardiac Anomalies of the Nervous System and Eye

edges.description: Hypertrophic, sometimes obstructive, cardiomyopathy arises in the NDUFB11 complex I spectrum that is allelic with histiocytoid cardiomyopathy. The edge is drawn from the shared subunit defect, not from the histiocytoid lesion, because the reported hypertrophic probands were not pathology-proven histiocytoid cases.

Chronic energy failure is followed by compensatory mitochondrial proliferation, lipid microvacuolation, and loss of contractile apparatus in affected cells. The steps linking the bioenergetic defect to the focal, conduction-system-biased distribution of the transformed cells are not established.

A subset of children present with dilated cardiomyopathy morphology and systolic dysfunction rather than with isolated arrhythmia; this entry attributes that presentation to the bioenergetic failure rather than to the focal nodules.
intermediate_mechanisms: Chronic ATP deficit in working myocardium with loss of contractile apparatus, giving progressive systolic dysfunction and chamber dilation.

edges.description: Transformed cells accumulate as multifocal, sharply demarcated clusters and nodules rather than diffusely, which is what distinguishes histiocytoid cardiomyopathy from a generalised mitochondrial cardiomyopathy.

nodes.description: The lesional cells behave as autonomous arrhythmogenic foci. Clinically this produces incessant ventricular tachycardia and short-coupled premature ventricular complexes that initiate torsade de pointes, typically refractory to standard antiarrhythmic drugs. Catheter mapping localises discrete triggering foci with recordable pre-potentials, and successful ablation or surgical excision of the foci can abolish the arrhythmia, directly implicating the lesions as the substrate. The response of otherwise-refractory arrhythmia to high-dose carvedilol has been proposed to implicate ryanodine-receptor store-overload-induced calcium release, but this rests on a single case.

nodes.description: The proximal lesion is a defect in a structural subunit of the mitochondrial respiratory chain. Two arms are established. In the mitochondrial-DNA arm a heteroplasmic MT-CYB missense variant (m.15498G>A, p.Gly251Asp) impairs ubiquinol-cytochrome c oxidoreductase (complex III). In the nuclear X-linked arm, de novo truncating variants in NDUFB11, an accessory subunit of complex I, abolish or reduce NDUFB11 protein and impair complex I assembly and activity. A minority of probands carry rare variants in other complex I components (NDUFAF2, NDUFB9), so the disease is genetically heterogeneous and remains unsolved in many historical cases.

nodes.description: The cellular hallmark of the disease. Affected cells are enlarged, polygonal, and pale, with abundant faintly eosinophilic foamy granular cytoplasm, coarse granules and microvacuoles, few or no myofibrils, and poorly developed or absent intercellular junctions. Ultrastructurally they are filled with excessive and aberrantly shaped mitochondria plus scattered lipid droplets. They are not histiocytes: immunophenotype and distribution identify them as modified cardiomyocytes with Purkinje/conduction-cell features, which is why the WHO 5th edition renamed the lesion "conduction system hamartoma".
